title: Doxycycline Loaded Collagen-Chitosan Composite Scaffold for the Accelerated Healing of Diabetic Wounds
protocol: Add 1.2 g of COL to 100 mL of water and keep aside for swelling.
Stir the swollen COL dispersion at 2000 rpm overnight to ensure complete dissolution of COL.
Prepare CS solution by dissolving approximately 0.8 g of CS in 100 mL of 1% acetic acid.
Stir the CS solution overnight at 2000 rpm to ensure uniform dispersion.
Mix DOX (1% w/v), followed by CS solution, to the COL solution, and stir for 30 min.
Filter the obtained physical mixture using a muslin cloth to remove particulate matter.
Deep freeze the obtained filtrate at -85 °C ± 4 °C for about 24 h.
Lyophilize the deep freeze mixture at -85 °C ± 4 °C for 72 h.
Store the obtained scaffolds in a desiccator for further analysis.
Dissolve MES (0.488 g) in 50 mL of water.
Soak 50 mg of the DOX loaded scaffold in 20 mL of the MES buffer for 30 min.
Mix 19.5 mL of MES buffer with 0.1264 g of EDC and 0.014 g of NHS in a separate beaker.
Immerse the scaffold in the buffer mixture for 4 h to achieve crosslinking.
Store the DOX loaded crosslinked (CL) and non-crosslinked scaffolds (NCL) for further evaluation.
Characterize scaffolds for morphological analysis using SEM (1 cm × 1 cm × 0.5 cm).
Stain the cross-section and exterior surface of the scaffold with a delicate layer of gold (~150 Å).
Capture photographic images at excitation voltages of 5 kV and 10 kV.
Place samples in aluminum stubs and enclose them with gold at approximately 9 V.
Measure the scaffold using SEM with increased resolution at 10 kV.
Determine porosity of the scaffolds using the liquid displacement method (ethanol).
Calculate porosity using the formula: Porosity = (Ww - Wd) / ρ × Wv, where Ww is wet weight, Wd is dry weight, and Wv is volume of the scaffold.
Measure the dry weight of the scaffold.
Incubate the weighed scaffold at 37 °C for 24 h in phosphate buffer saline (PBS) pH 7.4.
Remove excess PBS over the scaffold using filter paper.
Measure water absorption capacity using the formula: WS = (W1 - W0) / W0 × 100%, where W1 is wet weight and W0 is dry weight of the scaffold.
Incubate the scaffold (1 cm x 1 cm) at 37 °C for 7 days in PBS pH 7.4 containing lysozymes.
Wash the scaffold to remove any adhered ions on the surface.
Freeze-dry the washed scaffold.
Calculate the rate of degradation using the given formulae.
Disperse the scaffold in simulated wound fluid (pH 7.4).
Transfer the dispersed scaffold into a dialysis bag.
Tightly close the ends of the dialysis bag.
Immerse the dialysis bag containing the scaffold in 500 mL of simulated wound fluid solution.
Stir the wound fluid solution at 200-250 rpm.
Collect supernatant solution at definite time intervals.
Replace collected supernatant with an equal quantity of fresh buffer solution.
Determine the percentage of DOX release using a UV-visible spectrometer at 240 nm.
Prepare bacterial cultures using Mueller-Hinton broth at a ratio of 1:1000 to obtain 0.5 McFarland turbidity.
Add D-glucose (800 mg/dL) to bacterial cultures for hyperglycation.
Mince and solubilize CL and DOX-CL in DMSO (negative control).
Serially dilute hyperglycated bacterial suspension and test samples in a 96-well plate.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C for 20-24 hours.
Record the absorbance at a wavelength of 600 nm.
Sterilize scaffolds of standard dimension.
Place sterilized scaffolds in 24 well plates.
Add 3T3-L1 cells to the 24 well plate.
Incubate the plate with cells for 72 hours.
Feed animals with a high-fat diet for two weeks.
Administer a single dose of streptozotocin (STZ) at 50 mg/kg body weight in citrate buffer solution intraperitoneally to Wistar albino rats.
Choose animals with constant blood glucose levels of 250 mg/dL.
Randomize selected animals for excision wound induction.
Anesthetize diabetic rats using diethyl ether.
Confirm anesthesia using the toe pinch method and mucous membrane color.
Shave the dorsal area (dorsal thoracic, lumbar region) aseptically.
Sterilize the shaved area with an alcoholic swab.
Excise 2 x 2 cm² of skin to a depth of 1 mm with an aseptic surgical blade on the sterilized area.
Divide animals into three groups: Group 1 (Disease control), Group 2 (CL scaffold), and Group 3 (DOX CL scaffold).
Each group consists of 6 rats.
Affix the CL and DOX CL scaffolds using surgical tape.
Cover the control group with sterile gauze for 21 days.
Trace the wound area on a sterile OHP sheet.
Measure the percentage reduction of the wound using the grid method on days 0, 7, 14, and 21 for all groups.
Calculate the percentage wound reduction.
Isolate the healed wound area on days 7, 14, and 21.
Store the isolated tissue in formalin solution (10%).
Section the tissues using a microtome to obtain a thickness of 6 μm.
Mount the sections on a glass slide.
Stain the sections using Hematoxylin and eosin.
Capture images under 40x magnification using a digital microscope.
Isolate the healed wound area on days 0, 7, 14, and 21 for evaluation.
Estimate the hydroxyproline content using the procedure described by Reddy G et al., 1996.
Isolate tissue samples from the healed wound area on day 21.
Mince the tissue samples using a tissue homogenizer.
Centrifuge the obtained homogenate and collect the supernatant.
Dilute the supernatant at 100-fold using assay buffer.
Estimate MMP-9 levels using the Elisa kit as per the manufacturer's instructions.
Scan the plate using a multiple plate reader.
Perform the statistical analysis using Graph pad prism v5.01.
Conduct One Way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA).
Use Dunnet's post hoc test for multiple comparisons.
Consider values with p≤0.05 as statistically significant.
